notes: The manual shows three diagrams: a two-leg button wired directly (GPIO17 + GND), a four-leg button on a breadboard, and two four-leg buttons sharing a ground rail. Only the last (most complete) is modelled, as the catalogue has no two-leg button type; the 4-leg button on GPIO17 is the first button.
Second button's input pin is GPIO5 (per the image, labelled GP5); GPIO 17 is the input for button 1 as stated in the text.
Ground wire goes to the Pi's GND at the third header row (physical pin 6), mapped to catalogue port GND.1 (assumed numbering by pin order).
Breadboard rail hole numbers (tn.1, tn.5, tn.10) are approximate positions on the left negative rail; the rail is a single strip so exact hole is irrelevant electrically.
Buttons straddle the centre gap: button rows 5/7 and 10/12; ground wire in column a of rows 5 and 10, GPIO wires in column a of rows 7 and 12. Button side 1 = ground row, side 2 = GPIO row.
